hide_existence.notes: Prefer hide-existence semantics aligned with TEN-1 and ERR-1.

AP-ASH2-DRIFT.ban: Using Ash 2.x API-centric abstractions as the primary boundary (e.g., Ash.Api) instead of Ash.Domain.

AP-DEDUPE-WITHOUT-ACCOUNT-SCOPE.ban: Deduplicating inbound provider events using only (provider, provider_event_id) without provider_account_ref.
AP-DEDUPE-WITHOUT-ACCOUNT-SCOPE.rationale: Prevents cross-merchant collisions when providers reuse event ids across accounts/environments.

AP-IMPLICIT-TENANCY.ban: Relying on ambient/process-global tenancy; org_id MUST be explicit in every public action context.

AP-KEY-NAMING.ban: Using api_actions naming in contracts; use domain_actions.

AP-ORGID-FROM-UNVERIFIED-PAYLOAD.ban: Deriving org_id (tenant) from unverified/mutable inbound payload fields for integration processing (webhooks, callbacks).
AP-ORGID-FROM-UNVERIFIED-PAYLOAD.rationale: Prevents tenant leakage and cross-account misattribution; org_id must be derived from authenticated credential context.

AP-PROVIDER-ID-WITHOUT-ACCOUNT-SCOPE.ban: Using a provider-native identifier (e.g., provider_event_id) for dedupe/identity without including provider_account_ref in both the Ash identity and the DB unique index.
AP-PROVIDER-ID-WITHOUT-ACCOUNT-SCOPE.rationale: Prevents silent cross-account collisions when the same provider issues identical IDs across separate integration accounts.

AP-RMW.ban: Read-modify-write for correctness-critical invariants; require atomic database predicates for money/inventory/idempotency.

changes: P0: Explicit tenant resolution rule (org_id from authenticated credential context; payload trust forbidden).
P0: Triple-key dedupe mandate (provider, provider_account_ref, provider_event_id).
P0: EVT-1 registry authority linkage for RP-0 produced events.
P0: Dependency floors raised to Physics-hardened versions (LOCKS-1@2.1.0, DP-1@2.1.0, SM-0@1.2.0, EVT-1@2.7.0, ERR-1@1.4.10, TEN-1@1.7.4).

optimistic_locking.notes: Use optimistic locks for high-contention updates; still enforce invariants via atomic predicates.

row_locks.notes: Use query locks only inside transactions; avoid long lock-holding transactions.

identities_and_constraints.notes: If an identity is globally unique across tenants, it MUST explicitly declare all_tenants? true and be reviewed under GOV-0.
identities_and_constraints.provider_id_scoping_rule: For any third-party provider-native identifier used for idempotency or identity, resources MUST include provider_account_ref and MUST incorporate it into identities and unique indexes. Unscoped provider IDs are FORBIDDEN.

identity.name: unique_event
identity.notes: Third-party provider event IDs MUST be scoped to integration account to prevent cross-account collisions.

required_attributes.notes: Opaque integration account reference derived from verified integration context; MUST NOT be client-controlled.

triple_key_mandate.text: Inbound provider events MUST be scoped and deduplicated by (provider, provider_account_ref, provider_event_id). Dedupe keys that omit provider_account_ref are FORBIDDEN.

timestamps.notes: All persisted timestamps MUST use utc_datetime_usec to preserve ordering correctness for events and audits.

dependencies.reason: Static lint rules for suite hygiene.
Multi-tenant identity, org_id lifecycle, RLS expectations.
Error codes and severity registry for protocol failures.
Ingress security + webhook durability + outbox requirements.
Bulkhead / pool isolation expectations for traffic classes.
CAS fencing requirements for state transitions.
Governed event registry and drift governance.

SEC-1.reason: SEC-1 defines provider webhook ingestion and ProviderEvent dedupe identity. RP-0 patterns MUST align on provider_account_ref scoping.

invocation_context_notes: tenant MUST be set via Ash multitenancy (strategy=attribute) using the org_id tenant key.
actor MUST be provided as Ash actor option; implementations MUST NOT trust client-supplied tenancy or actor fields inside request bodies.
request_id/trace_id MUST be injected into telemetry/log context; they MUST NOT be persisted as domain attributes unless explicitly required by a domain contract.

invocation_context_required.must_be_passed_as: Ash invocation context/options (tenant:/actor:/context), not action arguments, unless a field is true business data.

domain_actions.purpose: Define allowed design patterns for externally reachable Domain actions and internal actions.
validation_rules: External side-effecting actions MUST support Idempotency-Key and parameter-consistent replay semantics (LOCKS-1).
Action names MUST be explicit (create/register/open, update/edit/set, destroy/archive/retire).
List/read actions MUST expose explicit allowlisted filter/sort inputs to prevent query abuse.

audit_context_requirements.transition_audit_record: Internal audit record, written atomically with a successful CAS transition.
audit_context_requirements.event_posture: Transition audit records are not domain events; RP-0 does not authorize an EVT-1 event or outbox write.

event_registry_authority.text: RP-0 implementations that emit events MUST ensure those event types are registered in EVT-1 and comply with EVT-1 governance (including schema_governance pointers where applicable).

events_and_ordering.ordering: Per-entity ordering MUST be tenant-partitioned by org_id.
ordering_notes: Outbox dispatch MUST be implemented per DP-1 to guarantee exactly-once side-effect emission under retry.
Per-entity ordering MUST be tenant-partitioned by org_id.

migration_backward_compatibility.compat_strategy: Breaking changes to tenant key naming or timestamp/id conventions require major version bump.
data_backfills: If migrating from utc_datetime to utc_datetime_usec, backfill microseconds as 0 for historical rows and rebuild indexes.
rolling_deploy_safety: Idempotency-Key replay semantics MUST remain stable across N and N-1 versions.

never_owns: Subsystem feature semantics (orders, seats, scanning, payments, payouts).
Repo-wide scanning rules (delegated to LINT-0/GOV-0 governance-class bundles).
SLO budgets and queue policy definitions (delegated to OBS-1/OBQC-1).
out_of_scope: Migration choreography and runtime harness specifics beyond what can be asserted deterministically in CI.
owns: Resource structure invariants (attributes, identities, actions, policies, multitenancy declarations).
Multitenancy posture: org_id is tenant key; tenant required for tenant-scoped resources; global reads forbidden by default.
Authorization posture: Ash.Policy.Authorizer; default-deny; constrained break-glass under GOV-0.
Idempotency posture for retriable external mutations: Idempotency-Key semantics via LOCKS-1 patterns.
Timestamp + identifier conventions: UUIDv7 and utc_datetime_usec for persisted time fields.

summary:
Canonical Ash 3.x resource/domain guardrails for Ticketing: multitenancy via org_id, explicit Policies, atomic correctness, and ERR-1/LOCKS-1 alignment.

v3.1.0: Adds mandatory provider_account_ref scoping rules for provider-native identities (aligns with SEC-1 triple-key dedupe).

global_reads.ban_reason: global? enables cross-tenant footguns; only explicitly global resources may allow it under TEN-1.

tenancy.strategy_notes: Ticketing tenancy is strategy=attribute with org_id as uuid_v7; strategy=context is reserved for future explicit contracts.

tenant_resolution.text: For any inbound integration message (e.g., webhooks/callbacks), org_id MUST be resolved from authenticated credential context (validated secret/API key/verified provider account binding). org_id MUST NOT be trusted from mutable payload fields.

tenancy.tenant_set_invariant: Tenant MUST be set for every tenant-scoped operation; cross-tenant reads are forbidden unless explicitly authorized by a domain contract and audited.
tenancy.tenant_set_mechanisms_notes: This list is guidance only; the invariant is mandatory regardless of framework edge (HTTP, GraphQL, background jobs, etc.).
